title: Choose the look of njason.dev
question: One direction is assigned. Keep it, take the alternative, or ask for a new hand.

options.label: The circuit board
options.lineage: printed circuit boards: solder mask, silkscreen, gold pads, copper traces
options.thesis: The site is a dark teal circuit board; the live lab widget is the powered part, and traces carry you from it into the work.
options.viewport: Cover photo left, your name very large in the middle, the live board on the right outlined in cyan with a gold pin header; traces run from it down into the page.
options.risk: If the traces and pads are overdone it turns into a costume; they must stay quiet and only connect real things.

raised.raise: Hierarchy is depth: three mask shades (ground, panel, raised) do the work instead of borders or labels.
Every number is shown with its unit and its conditions, measured against one spacing grid.
One card, one statement: a selected card floods with its colour instead of gaining chrome.
One master grid governs every page; sections differ by content, never by layout improvisation.

options.label: The dusk line
options.lineage: Japanese rail at dusk, taken from your Fuji photo: rounded station badges, departure boards, line colours
options.thesis: The colours come from your photo (dusk navy, Fuji teal, peach sky); the live lab is a departure board and the timeline is three train lines.
options.viewport: An arched photo left, your name in a rounded gothic face, and the live lab as a departure board with Now, Queue and Temperature rows.
options.risk: A transit-map metaphor for a career is familiar; it works only if the line colours carry real meaning (education, work, teaching).

options.label: Glass partition wall
options.thesis: Projects as glass panes in a black grid, lit one colour at a time.
options.viewport: A wall of panes, one lit cyan for the live lab.
options.risk: Reads as an art piece, not a hardware engineer.
options.case: Fuses cleanly but recruiters and engineers don't see themselves in it; clarity is fine, identification is weak.
options.kept: One pane, one statement: selection floods the card with colour.

options.label: Alphabet storm
options.thesis: Your words turning into weather over a white field.
options.risk: Light, surreal and slow to read; fights the dark-only choice.
options.case: Loses both axes: no link to hardware, and the message gets harder to read.

options.label: Cracktro screen
options.thesis: Bitmap text over drifting star layers.
options.viewport: One ivory line of bitmap text over drifting dots.
options.risk: Exactly the 'too hacker' look you ruled out.
options.case: Loses both: hacker costume, and bitmap type hurts clarity.
options.kept: Hierarchy by depth: layered surface shades instead of boxes.

options.label: Oscilloscope bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: The site as a scope screen with a phosphor trace.
options.viewport: A green trace across a graticule.
options.risk: Green phosphor is the 'too hacker' look.
options.case: Identification is decent for engineers, but recruiters lose clarity and it reads as a costume.
options.kept: Everything measured: numbers always carry units and conditions.

options.label: Design annual plates
options.lineage: a design annual's printed plate section
options.thesis: Projects as printed plates with registration marks.
options.viewport: A white sheet with one plate and a stamp.
options.risk: Light, editorial and mono-labelled: three things already ruled out.
options.case: Loses both: it speaks to designers, not hardware engineers.
options.kept: Photographs stay untinted and uncropped where it matters.

options.label: Swiss poster wall
options.thesis: Every section a poster on one modular grid.
options.risk: Light and cold; red signal colour clashes with cyan.
options.case: Clear, but nothing about it says hardware or you.
options.kept: One master grid across every page.

canonCard.label: The standard dark developer portfolio
canonCard.thesis: What most developer portfolios ship, done well.
canonCard.viewport: Name and line on the left, live widget on the right, equal cards below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like everyone else's portfolio by design.
